summary: Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg (Dr. phil. 1829). He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg, Breslau, Bonn (from 1839; also Rektor), and Leipzig (c. 1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, and others, then earned a doctorate in theology at Munich. He held posts at Munich, Freising, and Munich and Freising Archdiocese.

Friedrich Zarncke was a linguistics scholar. He studied at Rostock and at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. After holding a post at Rostock, he became a privatdozent at Leipzig in 1852 and served as its Rektor (1869–1882).

Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1787–1790). He held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), and later posts at Vienna (1824) and Utrecht (1825).

Friedrich von Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and in Paris under Hamilton and Chézy. His academic posts included positions at Jena, the University of Cologne, and TU Dresden.

Friedrich von Spiegel was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena, learning under Rückert, Lassen, and Brockhaus, among others. He was professor at Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal was an Indology, philosophy, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University. He held academic posts at SOAS, the University of Amsterdam (professor 1962–1967), and UC Berkeley (professor 1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at the University of Munich. He held a professorship at the University of Bonn (1934), was at Munich (1936–1941), and held a chair at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (c. 1947–1969).

Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian positions at the Institut National Agronomique and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and served as administrator of the Bibliothèque Mazarine from 1874 to 1885.

Fu-shih Lin specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a post at Academia Sinica from c. 1994 to 2021.
Fuang Jotiko was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo and Mun Bhuridatta.
Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong, and later held a post at Tunghai University from c. 1955 to 1969.
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University and held posts at Fukuoka University and Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa and studied under teachers including Yusho Miyasaka and Geshe Sonam Rinchen. He is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Fumi Yao is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who holds posts as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned degrees at the University of Tokyo, studying under Hajime Nakamura and others. He was a professor at Tokyo and at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
Fumihiro Okada specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and holds a post as specially appointed associate professor at Minobusan University.

Fumimaro Watanabe was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto (Ph.D. 1976 under A. K. Warder). He held professorships at Kindai University and Aichi Gakuin University.

Fumimasa Fukui was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. He studied at Waseda University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Paul Demiéville, Max Kaltenmark, and Rolf Alfred Stein. He was a professor at Waseda University (c. 1978–2005).
